title: Coefficient cocycle for intrinsic open extension
statement:
For arbitrary schemes, finite commutative coefficient rings A, B, C and ring homomorphisms phi:A→B and psi:B→C, the canonical comparisons satisfy the following equation, with no boundedness, constructibility or properness assumptions. The functors and normalized associators are those of [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor] and [def-sp-reduction-direct-image-comparison].

theorem reductionOpenScalarCoefficientCocycle
    {A B C : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing C]
    [Finite A] [Finite B] [Finite C] (φ : A →+* B) (ψ : B →+* C)
    {X Z : Scheme.{u}} (j : X ⟶ Z) [IsOpenImmersion j]
    (M : proEtaleDerivedCategory X A) :
    (scalarExtensionFunctor_composition φ ψ Z).hom.app
        ((sfIntrinsicExtensionByZero j A).mapDerivedCategory.obj M) ≫
      (reductionOpenScalarIso (ψ.comp φ) j).hom.app M =
    (scalarExtensionFunctor ψ Z).map ((reductionOpenScalarIso φ j).hom.app M) ≫
      (reductionOpenScalarIso ψ j).hom.app ((scalarExtensionFunctor φ X).obj M) ≫
        (sfIntrinsicExtensionByZero j C).mapDerivedCategory.map
          ((scalarExtensionFunctor_composition φ ψ X).hom.app M)

proof.text: The inverse open scalar comparison is the left-adjoint uniqueness map for the scalar extension and open adjunctions. By the iterated mate identity its mate is the inverse tensor/pullback comparison. Invert the pullback coefficient cocycle of [lem-sp-pullback-scalar-coefficient-cocycle], then use the injective adjunction correspondence to obtain the inverse open cocycle. Invert again to obtain the open scalar cocycle. Finally conjugate by reductionOpenModel: naturality moves the scalar associator across the coordinate map, intermediate model inverse pairs cancel, and naturality of the final model inverse gives the intrinsic formula. The private Lean lemmas open_mate, open_cocycle_of_pullback and transport_cocycle prove these calculations.

proof_origin.place: Step 11: formal mate argument and transport through the normalized intrinsic open model
